items.headline: Riyadh airport hit a second time Sunday; Saudi vows to "respond decisively," Trump repeats US "may" join the fight
items.summary: Houthi forces struck King Khalid International Airport again Sunday evening (Oct 11) -- a day after Saturday's attack killed 12 and wounded 309 -- with an unidentified projectile sparking a terminal fire before Saudi air defenses intercepted a follow-up cruise missile. The Saudi-led coalition called Saturday's strike a "full-fledged war crime" and pledged a firm response; Trump told reporters "We may. We're going to look at it... we'll make a decision. We move very quickly" when asked if the US would join Saudi strikes on the Houthis.
items.actionable: Back-to-back strikes plus an explicit Saudi retaliation pledge raise the odds of a wider Yemen war with direct US involvement -- keep the silver/gold-miner hedge in place and avoid adding equity risk into Monday's open given the live escalation risk.

items.headline: Oil climbs in early Monday Asia trade as Mideast attacks stack up: Brent ~$105.10, WTI above $92
items.summary: Brent crude advanced 0.4% to $105.10/bbl and WTI opened above $92 in early Asian trading Monday as markets weighed the second Riyadh airport strike plus a fresh drone attack on a tanker near Oman's Sohar anchorage (outside the Strait of Hormuz) reported by UK Maritime Trade Operations on Sunday. Bloomberg's rolling oil-markets wrap flagged both the Saudi airport attacks and the tanker strike as the drivers of the move.
items.actionable: Oil holding a bid into the open keeps inflation/Fed-hawkishness risk alive ahead of Wednesday's CPI -- a headwind for rate-sensitive SGX banks/REITs even as it reinforces the case for the precious-metals hedge.

items.headline: Hormuz tanker attacks hit a wartime high; exports still ~40% below normal
items.summary: USNI News and CNBC report 11-12 tanker attacks in the week through Oct 9 -- the highest weekly total since the Hormuz war began in late February -- with exports through the strait at roughly 8.5 million bbl/day, about 40% below pre-war levels. Iran continues to say the strait stays shut until the US accepts its "seven conditions," even as a separate drone strike hit a tanker near Oman's Sohar anchorage Oct 11, showing attacks are spreading beyond the strait itself.
items.actionable: No change to the standing Hormuz thesis -- persistently constrained supply keeps a floor under oil and under the case for holding (not trimming) the silver/gold-miner hedge while the blockade remains unresolved.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan activate the Mecca mutual-defense pact against the Houthis
items.summary: Following an emergency meeting of defense and foreign ministers in Riyadh on Oct 5, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan invoked "collective deterrence measures" under the Mecca Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement (signed Aug 7) -- the pact's first-ever activation. Turkish and Pakistani forces are to deploy air-defense and other capabilities to Saudi cities and oil installations, freeing Saudi aircraft to concentrate on strikes against the Houthis in Yemen.
items.actionable: A three-country mutual-defense pact being activated for the first time signals the Yemen front is now treated as a genuine war footing, not a contained skirmish -- another structural support for the book's precious-metals tail hedge.

items.headline: Gold holds near $4,190-4,210, silver near $60-61 as Gulf risk stays bid through the weekend
items.summary: Spot gold traded in a $4,190-4,210/oz range Oct 11-12 and silver held near $60-61/oz, both well off January's records ($5,608 gold, $121.62 silver) but continuing to find a safe-haven bid from the dual Gulf flashpoints (Hormuz blockade plus the Houthi/Saudi airport attacks) heading into Monday's Asia open.
items.actionable: Directly validates the book's core long-vol precious-metals thesis; watch for follow-through (or fade) once Asia/SGX trading opens and reacts to the weekend's escalation.

items.headline: Trump pledges no US strike on Iran before the midterms, citing "productive" talks
items.summary: Trump said on Truth Social the US "will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to" the Nov 3 midterms, citing ongoing productive talks with Tehran, even as reports say the Pentagon has separately drawn up strike options that could be exercised before the vote. This caps, but does not remove, the direct US-Iran escalation tail -- it does not touch Iran's Hormuz blockade or the separate, still-live Houthi/Saudi front.
items.actionable: Removes near-term direct US-Iran strike risk but leaves both the Hormuz blockade and the Houthi/Saudi front open, so the precious-metals hedge rationale is unchanged.

items.headline: China lets provinces tap $82B in unspent bond quota in incremental growth push
items.summary: China's Ministry of Finance said Friday Oct 9 it will let provinces draw on roughly 550 billion yuan ($82B) of unspent bond quota saved from prior years -- including 300 billion yuan in general bonds for county-level spending -- as Beijing's latest incremental stimulus effort to hit this year's growth target. Analysts characterized it as a nudge rather than a game-changer, consistent with Beijing's pattern since September 2024.
items.actionable: Modestly supportive of China growth/risk sentiment into Monday's HK tech open, but the "nudge not game-changer" framing argues against reading this as a durable re-rating catalyst for the 0700.HK/1810.HK/0981.HK sleeve.

items.headline: Tencent, Xiaomi and SMIC lead Stock Connect volumes and buybacks into the weekend
items.summary: Tencent, Xiaomi and SMIC ranked #1-#3 by southbound Stock Connect turnover on Oct 9 (RMB 2.10B/1.997B/1.855B respectively), while both Tencent (HK$100M) and Xiaomi (HK$47.6M) executed fresh buybacks on Oct 5. Separately, SMIC is planning to break out AI-chip revenue as its own reporting line as soon as Q3 2026, after demand for AI-adjacent peripheral chips outgrew its existing consumer/smartphone/industrial categories.
items.actionable: Heavy southbound buying plus active buybacks across all three of the book's HK tech holdings signal continued institutional and corporate support into the new week, and the SMIC AI-revenue disclosure change would improve visibility into the book's highest-growth China tech exposure.

items.headline: Singapore mandates bail-in bonds for 7 systemic banks; DBS faces an estimated S$4.3B capital gap, while Singtel keeps its Buy rating after a 3Q beat
items.summary: Singapore's Parliament passed the Financial Services and Markets (Amendment) Bill on Oct 6, giving MAS statutory power to require the city-state's seven systemically-important banks to hold dedicated bail-in-able debt pools; DBS's gap versus the new requirement is estimated at roughly S$4.3B based on March 2026 figures. Separately, DBS, BofA and UOB all retained Buy/target S$5.46 on Singtel after its FY2027 Q1 underlying net profit rose 27% y/y to S$831M, with the Optus minority-stake sale talks (to infrastructure investor Morrison, >A$2B) still unresolved.
items.actionable: The bail-in mandate is a multi-year regulatory overhang on DBS's capital-return capacity (modestly bearish for buybacks/dividends), while Singtel's reiterated Buy ratings and the pending Optus stake sale remain a clear positive catalyst for the book's SGX telecom exposure.

items.headline: Lynas agrees to acquire Meteoric Resources for ~A$968M, deepening its ex-China heavy-rare-earth pipeline
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths signed a binding deal to acquire Meteoric Resources, gaining the Caldeira ionic-clay project in Brazil -- described as the largest known heavy rare-earth resource outside China. The deal comes as China's one-year suspension of its expanded rare-earth export controls (covering five additional elements and extraterritorial reach) is confirmed to run to Jan 10, 2027 following the Trump-Xi Washington summit.
items.actionable: Strengthens the ex-China heavy-rare-earth supply story underpinning the watchlist thesis as a structural hedge against any future China export-control shock; the Jan 10, 2027 truce expiry is the next date to flag for the watchlist.

items.headline: Ether ETFs post a 9th straight day of outflows as Solana funds snap a 14-week inflow streak; Bitcoin holds near $83K
items.summary: US spot Ether ETFs extended their outflow streak to nine straight sessions (part of ~$986M combined Bitcoin+Ether ETF outflows so far in October) while Solana funds saw their first weekly outflow after a record 14-week inflow run, per TheBlock. Bitcoin itself held relatively steady near $83,000 through the weekend even as the broader crypto-ETF complex saw net redemptions.
items.actionable: Bitcoin's resilience near $83K despite broad ETF outflows suggests the selling is rotational/profit-taking rather than a risk-off break -- worth monitoring into Wednesday's CPI print for any correlated move with the rates-sensitive miner book.

items.headline: CapitaLand Ascendas REIT tops institutional net-selling list with S$93.4M outflow
items.summary: CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR) was the most net-sold SGX stock by institutional investors in the week beginning Sept 28, per REITSWEEK, with roughly S$93.4M of institutional selling despite the REIT's S$20.1B diversified portfolio across Singapore, Australia, the US, Europe and Japan.
items.actionable: A sizeable institutional sell-down in one of the book's larger SGX REIT holdings is worth tracking for a trend versus a one-week rotation, particularly if the rising-yield pressure on SGX banks spreads into REIT valuations.
